note: Cheap power and TVA in the north, Alabama Power elsewhere; receptive utilities. Hot, humid climate and tornado exposure. First local moratoriums (Anniston, Westover) adopted Aug 2026.
Free cooling and water, but an isolated grid, very high power prices, seismic risk and almost no fiber ecosystem.

Phoenix is a top-tier market with roughly 100 operating sites. The 2026 budget (SB 1861, signed June 13) bars new data center applications for the sales tax exemption from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2029, and 113 applications rushed in during the last two weeks. Existing certifications are untouched, and the pause changes incentive eligibility rather than prohibiting construction. The Colorado River Tier 1 shortage, in place since 2022, trims Arizona's supply about 18% again in 2026. Backlash is now regulatory: Tucson adopted data center rules Aug 5, Pima County imposed a 120-day moratorium Aug 11, and Pinal County denied the La Osa rezoning Aug 26, 2026.

note: Low industrial rates and about $12B committed across four hyperscale campuses, including Google in West Memphis and Avaio in Little Rock, with the first expected to operate in 2027. Entergy Arkansas filed new large-load rate schedules with the PSC in February 2026. Organized local opposition has now emerged: more than 100 people packed a Conway city hall meeting over a proposed $1B campus advanced by a shell company for an unnamed client, and biweekly demonstrations followed. Six Senate resolutions that would have authorized data center legislation died at sine die in April 2026. Limited fiber depth and tornado exposure.

note: Unmatched connectivity but the highest industrial power price in the lower 48, transformer shortages leaving built facilities unpowered, and the first voter-approved citywide ban (Monterey Park, June 2026) plus a Coachella Valley restriction bloc. Seismic and wildfire risk.
Denver is a solid secondary market with cool, dry air. Xcel capacity is tight, Colorado River basin water stress is severe, and hail and wildfire losses are high.
ISO-NE power is scarce and expensive; Groton enacted a local moratorium. Low natural hazard exposure is the main upside.
PJM capacity pricing at the cap flows into Delmarva bills; Dover is weighing an 18-month pause and Harrington rejected a data center ordinance in Aug 2026.

Miami is a key interconnection hub for Latin America and FPL is building generation, but the 2026 Hyperscale Data Center Act raised the exemption threshold to 100 MW and at least eight counties adopted one-year moratoriums in mid-2026. Hurricane exposure is the worst in the country.

Atlanta is a top-tier growth market. Georgia PSC approved 9,885 MW of new Georgia Power generation in Dec 2025 mostly for large loads; the large-load pipeline reached ~69 GW. The sales tax exemption survived a repeal push and runs through 2032, but 28 local moratoriums (Savannah, Rockdale, Newton and others) make site entitlement harder.
By far the highest power price in the US and an island grid; not a development target.

Hydro-heavy power that is cheap regionally rather than nationally (7.69¢/kWh in 2024, behind New Mexico and Washington), a cool dry climate, and Meta's $1.2B Kuna campus, which began serving traffic on Sept 4, 2026 using closed-loop cooling. The server equipment sales tax exemption still exists but HB 315 (2025) narrowed it after March 1, 2025 to entities meeting investment and job tests. Water is the flag: April 2026 snowpack was the lowest since records began in the 1930s and the state declared a drought emergency. Idaho Power has no data center tariff, pushing loads above 20 MW into special contracts. Fiber ecosystem is thin.

note: Chicago is a top-five market, but ComEd's large-load queue holds 28 GW of requests against a 24 GW all-time peak, PJM's 2028/29 capacity auction cleared at the price cap, and Gov. Pritzker directed DCEO to stop signing new Data Center Investment Program agreements from July 1, 2026. Agreements signed before that date are honored, and no end date was set; the two-year figure came from his budget proposal. Great Lakes water is a strength.

note: The most incentive-friendly large state: a sales tax exemption running 25 years, or up to 50 for investments above $750M. Good Jobs First estimates the Amazon New Carlisle package at roughly $8.2 to $8.3B, almost all of it the long-tail exemption value rather than named credits, against $13.8B Amazon says it has invested there. Local pushback is now substantial: the city of Elkhart adopted a moratorium through Dec 2027, Indianapolis and Marion County did the same in August 2026, and bans now cover 12 of Indiana's 92 counties. HB 1333 passed the House but died in Senate committee; its revenue idea was enacted separately as HEA 1210, letting a host community collect up to 1% of the sales tax the center does not pay.

note: Abundant wind and an established hyperscale cluster: Microsoft in West Des Moines and Meta in Altoona, with Google's Iowa campus at Council Bluffs in the Omaha metro rather than the Des Moines area. MidAmerican markets to large loads and asks for ten-year contracts, though Iowa regulators treat the contract terms as confidential, so the terms cannot be checked against a posted tariff. Woodbury County adopted a 12-month pause in unincorporated areas in June 2026, joining similar measures in Johnson, Dubuque and Madison counties. Derecho and tornado exposure.

note: Evergy has spare capacity and the state offers incentives; Kansas City metro gives some ecosystem. Tornado and hail losses are high and western water is stressed.
Second-cheapest industrial power east of the Mississippi, LG&E/KU and TVA territory, incentives intact. Modest fiber depth; flood and tornado exposure.

Second-cheapest industrial power in the 2024 EIA data at 5.61¢/kWh, though the rate rose about 7.5% year over year and sat sixth cheapest at 6.75¢ by mid-2026. The LPSC approved three combined-cycle units totaling about 2,262 MW for Meta's Hyperion campus in August 2025, two at Franklin Farms in Richland Parish and one at Waterford in St. Charles Parish. Meta now describes Hyperion as 5 GW of compute and more than $50B invested in the region. Entergy filed for seven more units in March 2026, about 7.5 GW across all ten, fast-tracked by the commission with a final vote due December 2026. Intervenors are pressing for a prudence review. Hurricane and flood exposure and a hot, humid climate are the trade-offs.

note: The legislature passed the first statewide moratorium (LD 307); Gov. Mills vetoed it April 24, 2026 and the override failed, but LD 713 stripped incentive eligibility and the Jay mill project was halted in June. Bangor and Eastport have local bans.
Frederick County spillover from Northern Virginia, but PJM constraints, above-average power prices, a Baltimore moratorium and a proposed statewide pause (HB 120).
Expensive ISO-NE power with little headroom; no state incentive program. Cool climate and low hazard exposure.

Gov. Whitmer is the most pro-investment governor of the cycle (OpenAI Stargate 'The Barn' in Saline), with a 2024 exemption and a July 2026 Responsible Growth Pledge. But 35 local moratoriums are tracked, and DTE/Consumers generation is still catching up. Great Lakes water and a cold climate are strong.

Cold climate and abundant water; Meta (Rosemount) and Microsoft (Becker) anchor the market. The 2025 law kept the equipment exemption but ended the electricity exemption and added fees; Xcel capacity is the constraint.

Industrial power below the national average but mid-pack for the Southeast (7.66¢/kWh in mid-2026, against 6.44¢ in Oklahoma and 6.63¢ in Arkansas). Amazon's Madison County build was announced at $10B in 2024 and the statewide commitment has since grown to $25B and 2,000+ jobs, with another $12B added in April 2026. Compass is building eight halls in Meridian toward roughly 500 MW from Mississippi Power. Incentives came largely from a 2024 special session rather than a standing data center statute, and the law letting Entergy contract with Amazon outside normal PSC approval is now the subject of a ratepayer dispute. HB 1239 died in conference in 2025 and no data center incentive statute passed in 2026. Hot and humid, tornado exposure, thin fiber ecosystem.

note: Kansas City and St. Louis offer connectivity; incentives available. Peculiar enacted a local ban and Ameren/Evergy headroom is moderate.

CNBC's grid analysis puts Montana among the ten best-positioned states on price and reliability; cold climate helps PUE. The grid is small, fiber is sparse, wildfire and drought are the physical risks.
Public power (OPPD/NPPD) has been receptive; Google, Meta and Microsoft cluster around Omaha. Second-cheapest residential power nationally. Tornado exposure.
Reno and Las Vegas have established campuses and partial tax abatements, but Lake Mead sits at ~32% and Reno's water use is contested. Low seismic and storm losses.
Expensive New England power and no headroom; otherwise a low-risk cold-climate location.

The state froze its $250M AI data center incentive, then enacted the Data Center Fair Share Act (July 7, 2026) creating a separate rate class and requiring data centers to curtail before residents. 72 tracked local moratoriums, the most of any state. Strong NYC-adjacent connectivity.

Cheapest industrial electricity in the US (5.43¢/kWh in 2024) and second on CNBC's 2025 list of grids best positioned for AI load. Meta's Los Lunas campus anchors at ~3.8M sq ft, with roughly 500 adjacent acres bought in late 2025 and a further ~$800M expansion approved by the village in March 2026. Water is the live constraint and is tightening: Santa Fe County adopted an 18-month ban on July 1, 2026, legislators have said they will file a statewide moratorium in the 2027 session, and a researcher told lawmakers in September 2026 that state data center water use could rise from about 500 million to 23.6 billion gallons a year if every planned project is built. Fiber depth is thin.

note: Executive Order 62 (July 14, 2026) holds discretionary DEC permits for data centers of 50 MW or more in abeyance until the Generic Environmental Impact Statement is finished, framed as up to one year. It reaches state discretionary permits only, not local government approvals, and applications deemed complete before July 14 are exempt, as are facilities primarily used for manufacturing, research, education or medical care. The legislature's broader 20 MW bill (S10642) passed both houses but has not been delivered or signed, and awaits action by Dec 31. ESD's Community Investment Framework proposes $1M per MW as a starting point for negotiation, not a fixed levy.

Charlotte (150-day), Durham County (9-month) and Apex (12-month) passed moratoriums. Duke Energy headroom is tightening.

note: Cheapest commercial power in the country (7.19¢/kWh in 2024), abundant gas and wind, receptive utilities, cold climate and low hazard exposure. Applied Digital's Ellendale campus, now Polaris Forge 1, is fully leased to CoreWeave across 400 MW of critical IT load and engineered to scale toward 1 GW; the first 100 MW building reached service in November 2025. A second campus, Polaris Forge 2 at Harwood, is a $3B, 280 MW build leased to Oracle. The sales tax exemption is intact and its cost rose from $15.3M in 2024 to over $65M in 2025. A bill to penalize developers using nondisclosure agreements with public officials (SB 2406) died in the Senate on Sept 3, 2026. Very thin fiber and labor pool.

note: Third-cheapest industrial power and Google's Pryor campus; HB 2992 (effective July 1, 2026) requires large loads to fund their own grid costs. SB 1488 statewide moratorium and HB 4424 property tax rollback were proposed but not enacted; Oklahoma City passed a local pause. Tornado alley.

Hillsboro's cable landings and Prineville/The Dalles campuses are mature, but BPA transmission and PGE capacity are constrained and the 2025 POWER Act shifts costs onto large loads. Cascadia seismic risk; cool climate is ideal for cooling.

Second-highest power supply available for computing per CNBC, nuclear restarts and new gas, and Amazon's $20B commitment. Shapiro's GRID Standards (May 2026) make the sales tax exemption conditional on clean-firm generation, LEED Gold and 50 jobs at 125% of average wage. PJM capacity costs and many township-level fights.
Among the most expensive power in the lower 48 with no headroom.

The exemption covers both equipment and electricity for qualifying facilities, and Palmetto Sites readiness funding rose more than 250% to $80M in 2026 with 51 certified sites. Generation is the constraint rather than the draw: 2026 reporting puts South Carolina behind on generating capacity and on power available for computing, even with competitive rates and good water. The V.C. Summer restart is a roughly two-year feasibility study under Brookfield, not available capacity. The Data Center Development Act (S.867) got a favorable committee report in April 2026 but has not passed. Hurricane exposure on the coast.

note: On CNBC's best-grid list, but SB 135 / HB 1038 (2026) add disclosure and cost-allocation rules using a 10 MW threshold, and there is no dedicated incentive. Sparse fiber.

Industrial power at 6.21¢/kWh in the 2024 EIA data, which is a state average rather than a TVA tariff and had risen to about 6.8¢ by mid-2026 after a 4.5% TVA base increase. Tennessee scored in CNBC's top band for water availability and finished 9th overall in 2026. The data center exemption and the 1.5% reduced electricity rate survived the 2026 session unchanged. Public Chapter 961 (May 2026) is a cost-allocation law, barring utilities from absorbing infrastructure costs for centers over 50 MW and letting those centers self-generate. Oak Ridge and Nashville ecosystems. xAI's Memphis campus is here, though the live 2026 turbine litigation concerns Colossus 2 across the line in Southaven, Mississippi. Tornado exposure.

note: The largest pipeline in the country (roughly 1,000 projects under construction or planned) and Dallas is the second-largest market. Gov. Abbott's Aug 3, 2026 directive paused pending data center interconnections until each project passes a PUCT/ERCOT audit, with a report targeted for Dec 10. That pause runs through ERCOT's process, so it does not reach the El Paso, Panhandle and East Texas areas outside ERCOT, and the December target is an audit milestone, not a date when power becomes available. ERCOT was weighing ~474 GW of large-load requests (about 90% data centers) and halted Batch Zero classifications. SB 6 already allows curtailment of 75 MW+ loads. The sales tax exemption survives until at least the 2027 session. Water is strained statewide.

note: Executive Order 2026-03 (May 29) is a review framework rather than a moratorium. It directs executive-branch agencies, excluding higher education, the State Board of Education, the Attorney General, Auditor, Treasurer, Legislature and Judiciary, to apply a higher bar to large data center review, requiring that water consumption not increase and that Great Salt Lake impacts be weighed. It followed the 9 GW Stratos proposal in Box Elder County, whose referendum campaign is now in district court. Dry, cool climate and Salt Lake City connectivity remain positives.

note: Gov. Scott vetoed H.727's restrictions (May 28, 2026) and the override failed, but the grid is tiny and power is expensive. Lowest natural hazard exposure in the country.

Still the world's largest market (Northern Virginia ~13% of global capacity, 0.5% colocation vacancy and a majority of 2026 capacity already committed, per CBRE H2 2025) but the hardest place to get power: Dominion has quoted 7-year waits for 100 MW since 2024, had ~54 GW under contract by July 2026 and ~70 GW of requests in queue. The 2026 budget left the sales tax exemption in place through 2035 but added a $0.011/kWh electricity consumption tax from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2028, with revenue above $600M a year refunded. HB 153 requires a site assessment before local rezoning or special-use approval for 100 MW+ projects, and DEQ must define Cooling Water Scarcity Areas by July 2027. The price shown is the unadjusted 2024 EIA average and does not include the new consumption tax.

note: Cheap hydro and a cool climate put Washington atop CNBC's grid ranking; Quincy and Seattle are established markets. Grant County PUD is effectively full and BPA transmission is the bottleneck; the exemption is limited to rural counties; Snohomish County paused applications through Dec 2026.

HB 2014 (2025) created a certified microgrid district program letting data centers self-supply from coal or gas; Berkeley County is a Northern Virginia spillover. Rural opposition (Tucker County) is emerging; fiber is thin.

Microsoft (Mount Pleasant) and Meta (Beaver Dam) anchor a fast-growing market with a 2023 exemption and Great Lakes water. We Energies' gas buildout is contested and Port Washington-style local fights are frequent.

Gov. Gordon's EO 2026-03 ('Data Centers the Wyoming Way', June 3) explicitly keeps the state open for investment while making developers pay for new power; Cheyenne hosts a 1.8 GW Crusoe/Tallgrass campus. Cold, cheap, low-hazard, but very thin fiber and labor.
